title: Run-time Energy-Efficiency Optimization for AI and HPC Workloads
problem: Power management at exascale is critical for environmental/cost impact, but most methods require deep application knowledge.
motivation: GPU-dominated datacenters for AI/HPC need application-agnostic power optimization with minimal overhead.
method: The system watches code as it runs and uses spectral analysis (a technique that identifies repeating computational patterns) to detect which patterns recur during execution. For each pattern, it measures the GPU's energy consumption, then uses gradient-descent optimization (systematically testing frequency adjustments to find the best setting) to determine the ideal GPU frequency for that pattern. This saves energy because different computation patterns achieve different power-efficiency tradeoffs at different GPU speeds.
key_novelty: The innovation is optimizing GPU power consumption at runtime for any application—without needing to know its internal details—by detecting repeating patterns and tuning the GPU frequency separately for each one.
limitations: Limited to 'regular' applications; irregular workloads may not benefit; generalization unclear.
